<a id="acid_articulate"></a>
## Articulate: `13_acid_articulate.yml`

An acid house line played the whole way through, whose notes lengthen from short blips into
long, gliding, joined notes over each scene while its filter opens, with no gate changed. The demo sets Articulate on the scenes, on the line itself and as a generator that bounces between short
and long every bar, and a register bound to CC 74 opens the filter as the notes lengthen.

<a id="acid_glide"></a>
## Glide and Shorten: `12_acid_glide.yml`

Fluid acid techno for a synth with portamento: one sixteen-note acid line from start to finish,
and Glide and Shorten rows of 5, 7 and 3 steps putting its slides and short notes somewhere new
each bar, though the line itself never changes.

<a id="edm_density"></a>
## Density: `edm_density.yml`

A club track at 128 beats a minute in F minor whose every intro, build, breakdown and drop comes
from Density, which keeps a share of a clip's notes, the strongest places in the bar first. The
same seven patterns, each written at the busiest it will ever play, run through every scene, and
only the densities change: the scenes' own ramps fill the intro and the builds in and strip the
outro away, and four Shapes generators, sparse, half, rise and fall, each setting a Density, thin the breakdown, turn
the drums half time and make the arp and the lead trade places across the second drop.

<a id="mainstreet_hoedown"></a>
## Baroque Hoedown: `mainstreet_hoedown.yml`

An original Baroque hoedown for a synthesizer in the manner of Baroque Hoedown (Perrey and Kingsley). A
hoedown first, cheerful and bouncing, played on old synthesizers: a boom-chick bass and harpsichord,
a fiddle tune in sixteenths on a square lead, a baroque sequence round the circle of fifths, a
lyrical middle in the dominant key and a last time a step higher. No club effects.

<a id="microwave_snacks"></a>
## Synthesizer Novelty Tune: `microwave_snacks.yml`

An early-seventies synthesizer novelty tune in the manner of Popcorn (Hot Butter), with a tune of its own.
A popping lead of short notes that bounces through each chord, a bass on root and fifth, a second
part in the relative major with held strings, and a last time a step higher. Plain and dry, as the
early synthesizer records were.

<a id="nomore_nomore"></a>
## Eurodance: `nomore_nomore.yml`

An early-nineties eurodance song in the manner of What Is Love (Haddaway), with a melody of its own.
One loop throughout, i III v VII, a bar each: a stabbed organ riff, a bass on the offbeats, a kick
on every beat, a house piano in the choruses and a breakdown on the pad.

<a id="percussion_fish"></a>
## Drum and Bass: `percussion_fish.yml`

Drum and bass, an original: a breakbeat that keeps being re-cut, a reese bass, a darting tune, and a
school of hand percussion that gets a stretch to itself. An original piece, not a homage to any one
work. An introduction for pad and piano with the percussion arriving; the break; the first drop with
the reese and the tune; the same with the school of percussion; a breakdown; a build; a second drop
on a chopped bass and a re-cut break; the percussion alone with the sub; half time; the first drop
once more; and an ending for percussion and pad.

<a id="registers"></a>
## Registers: `20_registers.yml`

An acid techno riff of five notes, changed bar by bar by the four registers, AX to DX. AX, BX
and CX each move a different note of the riff, in cycles of 4, 6 and 5 bars, then all three
at once. Then DX fades the riff, kick and hat out together over six repeats of the last scene.

<a id="roll_d20"></a>
## Dungeon Synth: `roll_d20.yml`

Dungeon synth, an original: one theme carried through a tavern, a road, a crypt and a dragon, on the
sounds of an old keyboard pretending to be a medieval band. An original piece, not a homage to any
one work. A prologue for organ and bells; the theme on a recorder over a harp; the tavern, a dance
for harpsichord and recorder; the road, the theme as a march for horn; the crypt, organ and choir;
the dragon, a battle; the return, the theme with everything; an epilogue for the bell.

<a id="sailor_arpeggiator"></a>
## Arpeggiator: `11_sailor_arpeggiator.yml`

The verse of What Shall We Do With the Drunken Sailor, with its chords played through a different
arpeggiator in every scene: step lengths, orders, octave ranges and jumps, offsets, and then
combinations of them. The tune plays alongside, plainly, so you can mute it and hear only the
arpeggio.

<a id="sandworm"></a>
## Trance Builds by Density: `sandworm.yml`

A late nineties trance anthem in the manner of Sandstorm (Darude), its builds made by Density. A saw
lead hammers one note in sixteenths, the riff moved through i, iv, III and VII by a progression; a
kick on every beat and a bass galloping on the offbeats; a snare roll and the riff thickened by
Density before each drop; a long breakdown on the pad.

<a id="tie"></a>
## Ties: `08_tie.yml`

An original downtempo piece in D Mixolydian whose pad draws its chords with the Tie row rather
than with gates, so a chord lasts as long as the ties that follow it, and whose ending holds a
bass note with ties alone, longer than any gate could make it. The demo also brings in the tracks one at a time, morphs a tune into its answer, grabs an echo and slides a filter, so it's the closest
thing here to a finished song.
